title: How Germany’s Approach to Russia Backfired

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》旗下每日简报《DealBook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: 30 years ago, Germany put forth a theory for how to work with Russia that was supposed to keep Russia from going to war with its European neighbors.
sentences.zh: 30年前，德国提出了一套与俄罗斯合作的理论，旨在防止俄罗斯与其欧洲邻国开战。

sentences.en: Today, the story of how that theory not only failed, but backfired on Germany.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲述这个理论不仅失败，反而对德国造成反噬的故事。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Berlin Bureau Chief
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事，柏林分社社长

sentences.en: Katrin Benholz.
sentences.zh: 卡特琳·本霍尔茨。

sentences.en: It's Friday, April 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月8日，星期五。

sentences.en: Katrin, over the past few days, as evidence has emerged of Russian atrocities in Ukraine, the Western world has been looking for the next logical way to punish Russia.
sentences.zh: 卡特琳，过去几天里，随着俄罗斯在乌克兰暴行的证据不断浮现，西方世界一直在寻找惩罚俄罗斯的下一个合乎逻辑的方法。

sentences.en: And everybody keeps returning to the same place, which is shutting off the flow of energy from Russia to Europe and to
sentences.zh: 每个人都不断回到同一个点上，那就是切断从俄罗斯流向欧洲，特别是流向

sentences.en: Germany specifically.
sentences.zh: 德国的能源供应。

sentences.en: And so that's what we want to talk about with you.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们想和你讨论的话题。

sentences.en: Why does that keep coming up as a way of inflicting pain on Russia?
sentences.zh: 为什么这总是被提出来作为惩罚俄罗斯的一种手段？

sentences.en: Michael, Russia completely relies on the money that it earns on its natural resources, oil, gas, even coal.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，俄罗斯完全依赖其自然资源——石油、天然气，甚至煤炭——所赚取的资金。

sentences.en: And the European Union as a whole has been buying a lot of all of these things from Russia.
sentences.zh: 而整个欧盟一直在大量购买俄罗斯的这些资源。

sentences.en: Germany in particular gets about a quarter of its entire energy supply from Russia.
sentences.zh: 德国尤其如此，其全部能源供应中约有四分之一来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: About half the coal experts, you know, in Germany come from Russia.
sentences.zh: 德国大约一半的煤炭进口来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Some of that is oil.
sentences.zh: 石油方面也是如此。

sentences.en: That's about a third.
sentences.zh: 大约占三分之一。

sentences.en: And over half of German gas imports have been coming from Russia.
sentences.zh: 德国一半以上的天然气进口都来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: So Germany is basically Russia's most lucrative client in Europe for energy and especially for gas.
sentences.zh: 所以，德国基本上是俄罗斯在欧洲最赚钱的能源客户，尤其是天然气方面。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, if you put it all together, Germany pays Russia 200 million euros a day, roughly, in energy payments.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你把这些加起来，德国每天大约要向俄罗斯支付2亿欧元的能源费用。

sentences.en: So the reason people are calling for Germany to shut off the energy coming from Russia is because
sentences.zh: 所以人们呼吁德国切断来自俄罗斯的能源，原因就在于

sentences.en: that flow of energy is one of the biggest remaining sources of revenue for Russia at a time when they're being sanctioned left and right.
sentences.zh: 在俄罗斯四面受制裁的情况下，这股能源流是其仅存的最大收入来源之一。

sentences.en: This remains a way for Russia to basically pay for the war.
sentences.zh: 这依然是俄罗斯为战争买单的一种方式。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I mean, Russia is selling energy across the world, not just to Europe, but Europe is an important source of revenue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，俄罗斯向全世界出售能源，不仅仅是卖给欧洲，但欧洲是一个重要的收入来源。

sentences.en: And Germany within Europe is the biggest source of revenue revenue for gas exports for Russia.
sentences.zh: 而在欧洲内部，德国是俄罗斯天然气出口最大的收入来源。

sentences.en: So, you know, the focus has been very much on this one pipeline,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，焦点非常集中在这条管道上，

sentences.en: Nord Stream 1, which is a pipeline that carries most of the gas that Germany uses and in many ways has
sentences.zh: “北溪1号”，这条管道输送了德国使用的大部分天然气，在许多方面它已经

sentences.en: become a symbol of, you know, Germany's reliance on Russia for gas, but also this stream of energy revenue flowing the other way to Russia.
sentences.zh: 成为德国依赖俄罗斯天然气的象征，同时也象征着这股能源收入流向俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Katrin, why not just turn off that pipeline, as you say, this symbol of money leaving Germany and going to Russia at a time when it may be committing war crimes?
sentences.zh: 那么，卡特琳，为什么不直接关掉那条管道呢？正如你所说，在俄罗斯可能犯下战争罪的时候，这象征着资金从德国流向俄罗斯。

sentences.en: The problem, Michael, is that over the last 20 years, Germany has made itself incredibly dependent on Russia.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，迈克尔，在过去的20年里，德国让自己变得极其依赖俄罗斯。

sentences.en: This pipeline carries about 60 billion cubic meters of gas every year.
sentences.zh: 这条管道每年输送约600亿立方米的天然气。

sentences.en: It's also more than half of the entire gas that the German economy uses to keep humming.
sentences.zh: 这超过了德国经济维持运转所需天然气总量的一半。

sentences.en: Many manufacturers, you know, a lot of the sort of German companies that contribute to this being
sentences.zh: 许多制造商，你知道，很多德国公司之所以能成为

sentences.en: an export champion in the world, these companies use gas to power their production.
sentences.zh: 世界出口冠军，正是因为这些公司使用天然气来驱动生产。

sentences.en: So this pipeline, which carries the gas to Germany, is something that in a way represents this.
sentences.zh: 所以这条向德国输送天然气的管道，在某种程度上代表了这一点。

sentences.en: Politicians at the moment say, we simply cannot cut off the gas right now.
sentences.zh: 政客们目前表示，我们现在根本无法切断天然气供应。

sentences.en: They're scrambling to become more independent, but right now they say, we can't do it.
sentences.zh: 他们正在努力变得更加独立，但目前他们说，我们做不到。

sentences.en: So if you turn off this pipeline, you basically turn off the German economy.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你关掉这条管道，基本上就等于关掉了德国经济。

sentences.en: That's the thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前的想法。

sentences.en: Or at least it would take a very serious hit.
sentences.zh: 或者至少会遭受非常严重的打击。

sentences.en: So a lot of people are worried about this.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人对此感到担忧。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is, you know, normally you've got these economists who work for labor unions,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，你知道，通常情况下，那些为工会工作的经济学家，

sentences.en: and you've got economists, you know, who work for the Business Federation, and they don't tend to agree on everything.
sentences.zh: 还有那些为商业联合会工作的经济学家，他们往往不会在所有事情上达成一致。

sentences.en: But in this case, they absolutely agree.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，他们完全一致。

sentences.en: They say that turning off the gas right now to punish Russia would be catastrophic for the German economy.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，为了惩罚俄罗斯而立即切断天然气供应，对德国经济来说将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: They're talking about a six-point decline to GDP, which is worse than anything that we've seen for quite a while, including,
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是GDP下降6个百分点，这比我们很长一段时间以来看到的任何情况都要糟糕，包括

sentences.en: you know, the first year of the COVID pandemic, and in a similar ballpark to the financial crisis after 2008.
sentences.zh: 你知道，新冠疫情的第一年，其严重程度与2008年后的金融危机相当。

sentences.en: — So, Katrin, how is it that Germany has become this dependent on Russia for something as essential to its economic well-being as gas?
sentences.zh: ——那么，卡特琳，德国是如何变得如此依赖俄罗斯，以至于在天然气这种对其经济福祉至关重要的资源上受制于人？

sentences.en: Where does that story begin?
sentences.zh: 这个故事从何开始？

sentences.en: — You probably have to go back to reunification, Michael, when Western Germany and Eastern Germany,
sentences.zh: ——你可能得回到两德统一时期，迈克尔，当时西德和东德，

sentences.en: which was, you know, a communist country that belonged to the Soviet sphere of influence, became one country again.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个属于苏联势力范围的共产主义国家，重新成为了一个国家。

sentences.en: The Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
sentences.zh: 柏林墙在1989年倒塌了。

sentences.en: And there was the sense that peace in Europe was now a given.
sentences.zh: 当时人们认为欧洲的和平现在是理所当然的。

sentences.en: There was a huge ambition to sort of include Russia into what, you know, German politicians
sentences.zh: 人们有一种巨大的雄心，想要把俄罗斯纳入德国政客

sentences.en: sometimes call the House of Europe, you know, engage with Russia, trade with Russia, bind Russia to Europe through economic interactions.
sentences.zh: 有时所说的“欧洲之家”，即与俄罗斯接触、与俄罗斯贸易，通过经济互动将俄罗斯与欧洲捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: And the Germans were particularly keen on this, partly because, you know, there is a history of guilt dating back to the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 德国人对此尤为热衷，部分原因是，你知道，这有着追溯到二战时期的负罪感。

sentences.en: — Guilt over what?
sentences.zh: ——对什么感到内疚？

sentences.en: — Guilt over 27 million Soviet deaths as they came and liberated Germany from the Nazis.
sentences.zh: ——对2700万苏联人在解放德国、打败纳粹的过程中牺牲感到内疚。

sentences.en: And in the German psyche, often Soviet kind of equals Russian.
sentences.zh: 在德国人的心理中，苏联往往等同于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And so there is a sense that we owe them, and we certainly owe it to ourselves that there shall never be a kind of an aggressive, a confrontational relationship with Russia.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们有一种感觉，我们亏欠他们，而且我们当然也亏欠自己，绝不能与俄罗斯建立那种对抗性的关系。

sentences.en: It's bad for everybody.
sentences.zh: 这对大家都不好。

sentences.en: So given all these dynamics and all these complicated sort of historical feelings,
sentences.zh: 所以考虑到所有这些动态和所有这些复杂的历史情感，

sentences.en: you know, Germany really kind of developed this philosophy that after the fall of communism,
sentences.zh: 你知道，德国确实发展出了一种哲学，即在共产主义倒台后，

sentences.en: as Russia became a democracy and the hope was that it would sort of grow closer to the West,
sentences.zh: 随着俄罗斯成为一个民主国家，人们希望它能更接近西方，

sentences.en: that engaging it in trade and becoming more interdependent, Germany onto Russia and Russia on Germany, that this would further peace on the continent and bring prosperity to all.
sentences.zh: 通过贸易往来和相互依存——德国依赖俄罗斯，俄罗斯依赖德国——这将促进欧洲大陆的和平，并为所有人带来繁荣。

sentences.en: There was this sort of idea.
sentences.zh: 当时就是有这种想法。

sentences.en: — Well, just to make sure I understand that logic, it's that if Russia is economically linked
sentences.zh: ——为了确保我理解这个逻辑，是不是说如果俄罗斯在经济上与德国以及欧洲其他地区挂钩，

sentences.en: to Germany and to the rest of Europe, but especially to Germany because it's the biggest economy in
sentences.zh: 尤其是与德国挂钩，因为它是欧洲最大的经济体，

sentences.en: Europe, then Russia acts democratically and acts peacefully towards the rest of Europe.
sentences.zh: 那么俄罗斯就会表现得民主，并对欧洲其他地区表现得和平？

sentences.en: — That's right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: — So how does that thinking play out in practice?
sentences.zh: ——那么这种想法在实践中是如何体现的呢？

sentences.en: — So in the 1990s, after the war came down, Germany and Russia start trading much more.
sentences.zh: ——在20世纪90年代，柏林墙倒塌后，德国和俄罗斯开始进行更多的贸易。

sentences.en: And one of the clearest manifestations of, you know, a kind of future commitment almost to Russia is that people start talking about a pipeline that directly connects
sentences.zh: 而对俄罗斯未来承诺最明显的体现之一，就是人们开始谈论一条直接连接

sentences.en: the two countries.
sentences.zh: 两国的管道。

sentences.en: Now, gas had been running from Russia to Germany for a long time, and it had been coming through these underground pipelines that, you know, went through other countries, including
sentences.zh: 天然气从俄罗斯输往德国已经很久了，而且一直是通过那些地下管道输送的，你知道，经过其他国家，包括

sentences.en: Ukraine and Poland and then, you know, lined up in Germany.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰和波兰，然后到达德国。

sentences.en: But now they were talking about a pipeline that went direct from Russia to Germany.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们谈论的是一条直接从俄罗斯通往德国的管道。

sentences.en: And they called it Nord Stream 1, which is this incredibly ambitious project, an undersea pipeline, nearly 800 miles long, you know, serious feat of engineering that
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“北溪1号”，这是一个极其雄心勃勃的项目，一条近800英里长的海底管道，这是一项了不起的工程壮举，

sentences.en: would link Russia to Germany directly bypassing these, you know, other pipelines that exist over land and give Germany direct access to Russian gas.
sentences.zh: 它将俄罗斯与德国直接连接起来，绕过现有的陆上管道，让德国可以直接获得俄罗斯的天然气。

sentences.en: And so this was sort of proof that Germany meant business long term, because this was a long term, incredibly expensive, complicated undertaking.
sentences.zh: 这证明了德国是长期认真的，因为这是一个长期、极其昂贵且复杂的工程。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest champions at the time of this pipeline was Germany's chancellor,
sentences.zh: 当时这条管道最大的支持者之一是德国总理，

sentences.en: Gerhard Schroeder.
sentences.zh: 格哈德·施罗德。

sentences.en: And he really hit it off with this new Russian president, Vladimir Putin,
sentences.zh: 他和这位新任俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京一见如故，

sentences.en: who only a year after he was elected comes to speak to the German parliament.
sentences.zh: 普京在当选仅一年后就来到德国议会发表演讲。

sentences.en: It's the first time a Russian president has ever addressed the German parliament.
sentences.zh: 这是俄罗斯总统首次在德国议会发表讲话。

sentences.en: This is a big moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的时刻。

sentences.en: And what's more, this guy used to be a KGB officer in Dresden, so he speaks fluent German.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，这家伙曾经是德累斯顿的克格勃军官，所以他能说一口流利的德语。

sentences.en: He charms the entire German establishment by standing up in parliament and speaking in German,
sentences.zh: 他通过站在议会大厅用德语演讲，赢得了整个德国政界的青睐，

sentences.en: speaking in what he himself during that speech called the language of Goethe, Schiller and Kant,
sentences.zh: 他用自己在演讲中称之为歌德、席勒和康德的语言进行交流，

sentences.en: you know, referring to like two of the most famous poets in Germany and a famous philosopher.
sentences.zh: 你知道，指的是德国最著名的两位诗人和一位哲学家。

sentences.en: So he really puts it on.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you look back over that speech, it's striking.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你回顾那次演讲，会发现它非常引人注目。

sentences.en: It almost seems like everything that
sentences.zh: 似乎德国人在20世纪90年代所希望的一切，

sentences.en: Germans had hoped for in the 1990s, binding Russia closer to Germany, giving an incentive to become more
sentences.zh: 将俄罗斯与德国紧密联系在一起，激励它变得更加民主，并与西方进行贸易，

sentences.en: democratic and to engage in sort of trade with the West, that all this was actually panning out nicely.
sentences.zh: 这一切似乎都在顺利进行。

sentences.en: You know, he was talking to parliamentarians.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他当时正在与议员们交谈。

sentences.en: He was saying,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: Russia is a friendly European nation.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯是一个友好的欧洲国家。

sentences.en: He was actually talking about stable peace on this continent and how it's a quote, paramount goal for our nation.
sentences.zh: 他实际上谈到了欧洲大陆的稳定和平，以及这如何成为“我们国家至高无上的目标”。

sentences.en: He went so far as to actually describe, quote, democratic rights and freedoms as the key goal of
sentences.zh: 他甚至进一步将“民主权利和自由”描述为俄罗斯国内政策的关键目标。

sentences.en: Russia's domestic policy.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，从保守党到社会民主党的议员们都被深深吸引了。

sentences.en: So you can imagine members of the parliament from the conservatives all the way to the Social Democrats were riveted.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那天他获得了全场起立鼓掌。

sentences.en: In fact, he got a standing ovation that day.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 他似乎体现了这个后冷战时代的世界和欧洲，在这个世界里，与俄罗斯的和平不仅是可能的，而且实际上是一种长期的前景。

sentences.en: He kind of seemed to embody this post-Cold War world and Europe in which peace with Russia was not just possible, but actually kind of a long-term prospect.
sentences.zh: 所以“以贸易换和平”，这种认为给俄罗斯钱会使其成为更好参与者的哲学。

sentences.en: So trade for peace, this philosophy that money to Russia will make it a better actor.
sentences.zh: 这一切似乎都在奏效。

sentences.en: This all seems to be working.
sentences.zh: 听起来这在普京来到德国的那次演讲中得到了充分体现，他说，我来了，我是你们的伙伴，正如你们所希望的那样。

sentences.en: And it's very much embodied, it sounds like, you're saying, in this speech where Putin comes to Germany and says, here I am, your partner, just the way you want me to be.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，又过了几年，2005年，施罗德签署了“北溪1号”合同。

sentences.en: And you know, it would take another few years, but in 2005, this Nord Stream 1 contract is signed by Schroeder.
sentences.zh: 当施罗德的继任者上任时，她是安格拉·默克尔。

sentences.en: And when Schroeder's successor comes into office, it's Angela Merkel.
sentences.zh: 她是保守派。

sentences.en: And she's a conservative.
sentences.zh: 所以她来自一个完全不同的政党，在很多事情上都与施罗德意见不合。

sentences.en: So she's from a totally different party and disagrees with Schroeder and lots of things.
sentences.zh: 但在一点上，他们似乎完全一致，那就是对俄政策。

sentences.en: But on one thing, they're totally aligned, it seems, and that is the Russia policy.
sentences.zh: 她实际上是在2011年最终开启了“北溪1号”。

sentences.en: She's the one who actually ends up opening Nord Stream 1 in 2011.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，默克尔总理。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Chancellor Merkel.
sentences.zh: 确实，您可以就位操作转轮了。

sentences.en: Indeed, you may take your place at the wheel.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们，各位阁下，我们来到了仪式的最高潮。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, excellencies, we've come to the high point of our ceremony.
sentences.zh: 我们要转动历史的转轮。

sentences.en: We're going to turn the wheel of history.
sentences.zh: 我们需要……

sentences.en: We need...
sentences.zh: 她前往波罗的海。

sentences.en: She travels up to the Baltic Sea.
sentences.zh: 现在我请您把手放在转轮上，但先不要转动。

sentences.en: So now I will ask you to put your hands on the wheel, but don't turn it yet.
sentences.zh: 好的，先不要转动。

sentences.en: Okay, don't turn it yet.
sentences.zh: 她与其他几位欧洲领导人以及俄罗斯总统一起，转动了那个象征性的阀门。

sentences.en: And kind of turns the proverbial spigot with several other European leaders and also the
sentences.zh: 当时拍下了照片，他们都站在一起，你知道，转动着那个转轮，看起来非常高兴。

sentences.en: Russian president.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来觉得这是一件非常好的事情。

sentences.en: And there's photos of the occasion and they're all standing there together, you know, turning that wheel, looking incredibly happy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，安格拉·默克尔对这种与俄罗斯的天然气相互依存的想法深信不疑，

sentences.en: They're looking like this is a very good thing.
sentences.zh: 以至于同年她宣布要彻底淘汰核能。

sentences.en: And Angela Merkel is in fact so convinced by this idea of this gas, you know, interdependence
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: with Russia that that same year announces that she wants to phase out nuclear power altogether.
sentences.zh: 那一年发生了日本福岛核灾难。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 德国人从来都不喜欢核能，但这次灾难确实让公众舆论更加反对核能。

sentences.en: This is the year of the Fukushima disaster in Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以安格拉·默克尔决定我们要淘汰核能。

sentences.en: Germans have never been crazy about nuclear power, but this particular disaster really turned public opinion against nuclear power even more.
sentences.zh: 她在“北溪1号”开通的同一年做出了这个决定，这在某种程度上表明了她显然是多么信任这个能源来源。

sentences.en: And so Angela Merkel decides we're going to phase out nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 她做到了。

sentences.en: And she does it that same year that Nord Stream 1 opens, which sort of shows how reliable she clearly believed this source of energy was.
sentences.zh: 这显示出她显然认为这个能源来源是多么可靠。

sentences.en: So even Angela Merkel, who was never blue eyed and sort of delusional about Vladimir Putin, thought that this gas supply was something you could rely on pretty much forever.
sentences.zh: 所以，就连从未对弗拉基米尔·普京抱有幻想、甚至可以说对他有些误解的安格拉·默克尔，也认为这种天然气供应是可以长期依赖的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in the process, Merkel, of course, is deepening Germany's reliance on this gas pipeline from Russia.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，默克尔当然也加深了德国对这条俄罗斯天然气管道的依赖。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Germany was relying on nuclear for 25 percent of its electricity generation.
sentences.zh: 德国曾有25%的电力供应依赖核能。

sentences.en: So with that on its way out, gas became even more important.
sentences.zh: 随着核能逐渐退出，天然气变得更加重要了。

sentences.en: And in fact, at that time, they were already planning a second pipeline in the same place, which they were going to call Nord Stream 2.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当时他们已经在同一地点规划了第二条管道，也就是后来所说的“北溪2号”。

sentences.en: But then in 2014, Russia invades Crimea.
sentences.zh: 但随后在2014年，俄罗斯入侵了克里米亚。

sentences.en: And this was a moment really when Germany's allies for the first time seriously began to question this reliance on Russian gas and began to question the wisdom of
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个转折点，德国的盟友们第一次开始认真质疑这种对俄罗斯天然气的依赖，并开始质疑

sentences.en: signing up for a second pipeline.
sentences.zh: 签署第二条管道协议的明智性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because when Putin invades Crimea, it suggests that this German philosophy you have
sentences.zh: 因为当普京入侵克里米亚时，这表明你刚才描述的那种德国哲学，卡特琳，

sentences.en: been describing, Katrin, that trade makes Russia a more peaceful country might not be entirely correct.
sentences.zh: 即贸易能让俄罗斯成为一个更和平的国家，可能并不完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So this was kind of the first wake up call.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是第一次警钟。

sentences.en: And it does jolt the German establishment.
sentences.zh: 它确实让德国政界感到震惊。

sentences.en: There's no question that people are beginning to to think, you know, very hard about this philosophy of theirs.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，人们开始非常认真地反思他们这种哲学。

sentences.en: And this is when you begin to see very serious and vocal opposition from Germany's allies in Europe, but also in America.
sentences.zh: 这时，你开始看到来自德国在欧洲以及美国的盟友们非常严肃且直言不讳的反对。

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot of congresspeople who argue that Germany is making itself way too dependent, that Germany becomes kind of almost a hostage to the Kremlin,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多国会议员认为德国让自己变得过于依赖，德国几乎成了克里姆林宫的人质，

sentences.en: that Russia is now holding all the cards because Russia delivers the gas and controls that tap.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯现在掌握了所有主动权，因为它供应天然气并控制着阀门。

sentences.en: They warned Germany that Russia could weaponize the gas supply, that they could turn off the tap at any time.
sentences.zh: 他们警告德国，俄罗斯可能会将天然气供应武器化，随时可能关掉阀门。

sentences.en: And that very threat would mean that Germany could not act in the way that it needed to, because it was too dependent.
sentences.zh: 而这种威胁意味着德国无法采取它所需要的行动，因为它太依赖对方了。

sentences.en: Germany kind of said, we don't believe that.
sentences.zh: 德国当时的态度是，我们不相信会这样。

sentences.en: The Russians have always been reliable with their gas deliveries.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人在天然气供应方面一直很可靠。

sentences.en: And so they kind of reassure their allies.
sentences.zh: 所以他们算是安抚了盟友。

sentences.en: They say, we think this is fine.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们认为这没问题。

sentences.en: And Nord Stream 2 goes ahead.
sentences.zh: 于是“北溪2号”继续推进。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序，首月免费。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载时报应用程序，获取30天免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Katrin, once Russia starts to threaten Ukraine at the end of last year and into the beginning of this year, with troops on its border.
sentences.zh: 那么卡特琳，去年年底到今年年初，当俄罗斯开始在乌克兰边境集结军队并威胁乌克兰时，

sentences.en: How do Germany's leaders think about the place of these two giant gas pipelines in this emerging conflict?
sentences.zh: 德国领导人是如何看待这两条巨型天然气管道在这个新兴冲突中的地位的？

sentences.en: Germany was incredibly slow to really start talking about pipelines.
sentences.zh: 德国在真正开始讨论管道问题上行动极其缓慢。

sentences.en: I mean, as recently as January,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就在一月份，

sentences.en: Chancellor Schultz, who had, to be fair to him, just been in office for a month, still was talking about Nord Stream 2 as a, quote, private business project.
sentences.zh: 朔尔茨总理——平心而论，他当时才上任一个月——仍然称“北溪2号”是一个“私人商业项目”。

sentences.en: And so less than three months ago, this government still seemed wedded to the idea that they could just proceed with a further entanglement
sentences.zh: 所以就在不到三个月前，这届政府似乎仍然执着于这样一个想法：他们可以继续与俄罗斯进行更深层次的纠葛，

sentences.en: with Russia and that the pipeline should go ahead.
sentences.zh: 而且管道项目应该继续推进。

sentences.en: It was interesting when Schultz went to see President
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当朔尔茨二月份去见拜登总统时，

sentences.en: Biden in February and they stood there together for a press conference at the end.
sentences.zh: 他们在最后的新闻发布会上站在一起。

sentences.en: And Schultz was very directly and multiple times asked whether he was prepared to shut down Nord Stream 2 if Russia actually invaded.
sentences.zh: 朔尔茨被非常直接且多次问到，如果俄罗斯真的入侵，他是否准备好关闭“北溪2号”。

sentences.en: He said that he would take measures, but he didn't name the pipeline and he just dodged the question.
sentences.zh: 他说他会采取措施，但他没有点名管道，只是回避了这个问题。

sentences.en: It was actually President Biden who said if they invade, Nord Stream 2 is history.
sentences.zh: 实际上是拜登总统说，如果他们入侵，“北溪2号”就成为历史了。

sentences.en: And when Putin, a couple of days before the invasion, recognizes these two breakaway republics
sentences.zh: 而在入侵前几天，当普京承认乌克兰东部的两个分裂共和国——顿涅茨克和卢甘斯克时，

sentences.en: in eastern Ukraine, Donetsk and Luhansk, Schultz finally announces that Nord Stream 2 won't go ahead.
sentences.zh: 朔尔茨终于宣布“北溪2号”不会继续推进。

sentences.en: Just to be clear, this is Germany shutting down
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，这是德国关闭了

sentences.en: the pipeline that's not yet operational rather than shutting down Nord Stream 1, which is throwing tens of millions of dollars a day, we think, to Russia.
sentences.zh: 尚未投入运营的管道，而不是关闭“北溪1号”，后者我们认为每天都在向俄罗斯输送数千万美元。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Although it is the first step, the first sign that Schultz is acknowledging
sentences.zh: 尽管这是第一步，是朔尔茨承认

sentences.en: Germany had it wrong for 30 years.
sentences.zh: 德国过去30年都错了的第一个迹象。

sentences.en: And just a few days later, after Russia's actually invaded, it, Schultz stands up in Parliament and gives a 30-minute speech, where he basically announces
sentences.zh: 仅仅几天后，在俄罗斯真正入侵之后，朔尔茨在议会发表了30分钟的演讲，他在演讲中基本上宣布了

sentences.en: a complete overhaul of German foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 德国外交政策的彻底改革。

sentences.en: He announces that they would, after all, deliver weapons to Ukraine, another taboo, which had been unthinkable just a couple of days before.
sentences.zh: 他宣布他们最终还是会向乌克兰提供武器，这是另一个禁忌，而在几天前这还是不可想象的。

sentences.en: And crucially, he announces that Germany had to extract itself from its dependency in energy terms on Russia.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，他宣布德国必须摆脱对俄罗斯的能源依赖。

sentences.en: For a free and open, free and peaceful Europe.
sentences.zh: 为了一个自由、开放、自由与和平的欧洲。

sentences.en: We will defend it.
sentences.zh: 我们将捍卫它。

sentences.en: So this is a complete reversal of the philosophy,
sentences.zh: 所以这完全推翻了你所描述的

sentences.en: Catherine, that you described as taking root after German reunification in the early 1990s,
sentences.zh: 在1990年代初德国统一后扎根的那种哲学，卡特琳，

sentences.en: which says, get more and more bound up with Russia, because that will make Russia a more peaceful country.
sentences.zh: 即：与俄罗斯建立越来越多的联系，因为那会让俄罗斯成为一个更和平的国家。

sentences.en: This is Germany rejecting that philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这是德国在拒绝那种哲学。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: On that day in February, basically, Germany decided that it had been wrong about
sentences.zh: 在那一天的二月份，基本上，德国承认自己在军事政策上错了，

sentences.en: military policy, that it had been wrong about its foreign policy regarding Russia, and that it needed to change its energy policy.
sentences.zh: 在涉及俄罗斯的外交政策上错了，并且需要改变其能源政策。

sentences.en: It was kind of a complete rethink, and one that went pretty deeply to the kind of core of German post-governification identity, and to the core of the German business model.
sentences.zh: 这算是一次彻底的反思，而且深入到了德国统一后身份认同的核心，以及德国商业模式的核心。

sentences.en: But of course, this has to be a lot easier to say than to do, to suddenly stop being dependent on
sentences.zh: 但当然，说起来容易做起来难，要突然停止对俄罗斯的能源依赖，

sentences.en: Russia for energy, because as you've told us, Germany has gotten rid of its nuclear energy, for example, and its whole economy would collapse without Russian gas.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你告诉我们的，德国已经放弃了核能，如果没有俄罗斯的天然气，整个经济可能会崩溃。

sentences.en: It's incredibly difficult, Michael.
sentences.zh: 这极其困难，迈克尔。

sentences.en: And, you know, they are being tested almost every day, with more and more people pushing them to do more and move faster.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们几乎每天都在接受考验，越来越多的人敦促他们做得更多、走得更快。

sentences.en: And in some ways, they're moving remarkably fast, given that they've done nothing for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，考虑到他们长期以来什么都没做，他们的行动速度快得惊人。

sentences.en: But you can see, for example, that coal imports from Russia have already halved in just over a month.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看到，例如，来自俄罗斯的煤炭进口在短短一个多月内已经减半了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Oil imports, you know, have gone down pretty significantly from, you know, kind of a 35 to a 20 percent share in the total.
sentences.zh: 石油进口，你知道，已经从总量的35%左右显著下降到了20%左右。

sentences.en: Gas is harder.
sentences.zh: 天然气更难。

sentences.en: We've had ministers travel the world trying to sort of identify alternative sources, but they need so much of it.
sentences.zh: 我们有部长们奔走世界各地，试图寻找替代来源，但他们需要的量太大了。

sentences.en: So it's been incredibly hard.
sentences.zh: 所以这极其困难。

sentences.en: And you can imagine that the pressure is only growing.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象压力只会越来越大。

sentences.en: Last weekend, when these terrible images of the atrocities in Bucha, of these people, civilians lying dead on the streets, flickered across German television
sentences.zh: 上周末，当布查暴行的可怕画面——那些平民死在街头的景象——在德国电视屏幕上闪过时，

sentences.en: screens as they did across the world, that's when it really all blew up.
sentences.zh: 就像在世界各地一样，那时一切真的爆发了。

sentences.en: And Germans were being pressed by their allies, especially in Eastern Europe, to basically rise to the occasion and cut off the gas.
sentences.zh: 德国人正受到盟友，特别是东欧盟友的压力，要求他们挺身而出，切断天然气。

sentences.en: Even within Germany, the pressure is rising.
sentences.zh: 即使在德国国内，压力也在上升。

sentences.en: It's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: We've had critiques from neighboring countries for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 我们很长一段时间以来一直受到邻国的批评。

sentences.en: Within Germany, you're now seeing in very conservative newspapers, editorials that are basically talking about Germany's moral obligation, given its sort of
sentences.zh: 在德国国内，你现在在非常保守的报纸上也能看到社论，它们基本上在谈论德国的道德义务，鉴于其种族灭绝的过去。

sentences.en: genocidal paSt. So, you know, you've got this financial newspaper Handelsblatt, which had an editorial that said,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，财经报纸《商报》发表了一篇社论，说，

sentences.en: the country that proudly proclaims that Europe will never again see the likes of Auschwitz is pumping
sentences.zh: 这个自豪地宣称欧洲绝不会再看到奥斯威辛式悲剧的国家，每天都在向普京的战争金库

sentences.en: 200 million euros each day into Putin's war cheSt. You know, all of a sudden, this editorial says,
sentences.zh: 注入2亿欧元。你知道，突然之间，这篇社论说，

sentences.en: the discussion in Germany about whether our economy would grow by 6% or just 3% in the event of an energy embargo seems petty and insignificant.
sentences.zh: 德国国内关于能源禁运会导致经济增长6%还是3%的讨论，显得琐碎而无关紧要。

sentences.en: We resemble a hostage to the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 我们看起来就像克里姆林宫的人质。

sentences.en: I just want to talk about this editorial because it is very powerful, what you just read.
sentences.zh: 我只想谈谈这篇社论，因为它非常有力量，你刚才读的内容。

sentences.en: It seems to be asking, how can we, as a country that committed the ultimate war crimes, help finance a war in which another country is allegedly committing its own atrocities?
sentences.zh: 它似乎在问，作为一个犯下终极战争罪的国家，我们怎么能帮助资助一场另一国据称正在犯下暴行的战争？

sentences.en: It's an incredibly difficult question in this country.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，这是一个极其困难的问题。

sentences.en: And you can imagine the sort of moral debates that are raging right now.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象现在正在进行的道德辩论。

sentences.en: You actually have a majority of Germans by now in polls saying they would be prepared for their government to simply cut ties, cut the gas ties with Russia and shut off.
sentences.zh: 实际上，民调显示大多数德国人现在表示，他们准备好让政府直接切断与俄罗斯的联系，切断天然气供应。

sentences.en: But the government is arguing that they don't actually know what that would mean.
sentences.zh: 但政府辩称，他们实际上不知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Cutting off the gas would not just mean, you know, a massive rise in energy prices.
sentences.zh: 切断天然气不仅意味着能源价格的大幅上涨。

sentences.en: It would mean an increase in unemployment.
sentences.zh: 它意味着失业率的增加。

sentences.en: It would mean a recession that might be worse than anything we've seen for a couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 它意味着一场可能比我们几十年来见过的任何情况都更严重的衰退。

sentences.en: You know, Catherine, in thinking about the story that you have just laid out here,
sentences.zh: 你知道，卡特琳，在思考你刚才在这里阐述的故事时，

sentences.en: it really feels like the economic relationship that Germany pursued with Russia since reunification, since the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 感觉德国自统一以来，自1990年代以来与俄罗斯追求的经济关系，

sentences.en: It did not prevent Russia from doing bad things, which was the theory.
sentences.zh: 并没有阻止俄罗斯做坏事，而这正是当初的理论。

sentences.en: In fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: it has given Russia leverage that probably allowed it to invade Ukraine because it knew on some level that Germany could only go so far in punishing it without profoundly hurting Germany itself.
sentences.zh: 它给了俄罗斯筹码，这可能让它得以入侵乌克兰，因为它在某种程度上知道，德国在惩罚它时只能做到这一步，否则会严重伤害德国自身。

sentences.en: It knew how reliant Germany was going to be on its gas.
sentences.zh: 它知道德国对它的天然气有多依赖。

sentences.en: In other words, Putin figured out that this theory of interdependence in an area like gas, that could be a weapon that he could use against Germany,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，普京发现这种在天然气等领域的相互依存理论，可以成为他用来对付德国的武器，

sentences.en: not a weapon really that Germany could use against Russia.
sentences.zh: 而不是德国可以用来对付俄罗斯的武器。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no question that Germany got the balance wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问，德国在平衡上搞错了。

sentences.en: You get a scenario where basically you turned interdependence into a kind of dependence, which has kind of exposed a fundamental weakness in the story that not just Germany,
sentences.zh: 你陷入了一种局面，基本上你把相互依存变成了某种依赖，这暴露了不仅是德国，

sentences.en: but a lot of countries in the West, you know, that we pretty much all told ourselves after the fall of communism, after the end of the Cold War, that if you trade,
sentences.zh: 而且西方许多国家在共产主义垮台、冷战结束后都告诉自己的故事中存在的一个根本弱点，即如果你进行贸易，

sentences.en: if you make the costs of foregoing peace high enough, then you preserve peace.
sentences.zh: 如果你让放弃和平的代价足够高，那么你就能维护和平。

sentences.en: And it kind of works up to a point.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是有效的。

sentences.en: But, you know, that point is basically when you're dealing with autocracies like Russia.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这个限度基本上就是当你面对像俄罗斯这样的独裁政权时。

sentences.en: Well, Katrin, thank you very much, as always.
sentences.zh: 好吧，卡特琳，一如既往，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Thursday, in the latest effort to punish Russia, the European Union, including Germany, voted to ban the importation of Russian coal.
sentences.zh: 周四，在惩罚俄罗斯的最新努力中，包括德国在内的欧盟投票决定禁止进口俄罗斯煤炭。

sentences.en: But despite pressure from Ukrainian officials, the EU did not ban Russian gas.
sentences.zh: 但尽管受到乌克兰官员的压力，欧盟并没有禁止俄罗斯天然气。

sentences.en: In a statement, Ukraine's foreign minister said that as long as European countries continue to buy Russian gas,
sentences.zh: 乌克兰外交部长在一份声明中表示，只要欧洲国家继续购买俄罗斯天然气，

sentences.en: they are, quote, supporting Ukraine with one hand, while supporting the Russian war machine with the other hand.
sentences.zh: 他们就是“一手支持乌克兰，另一手支持俄罗斯战争机器”。

sentences.en: But we'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 但我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 53, the nays are 47, and this nomination is confirmed.
sentences.zh: 本次投票，赞成票53票，反对票47票，提名确认通过。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Senate voted to confirm Judge Ketanji Brown Jackson as a justice on the Supreme Court, making her the first black woman to serve on the nation's highest court.
sentences.zh: 周四，参议院投票确认凯坦吉·布朗·杰克逊法官为最高法院大法官，使她成为第一位在美国最高法院任职的黑人女性。

sentences.en: Jackson won the support of every Democrat in the chamber, as well as three Republicans who broke ranks with their party.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊赢得了参议院所有民主党人的支持，以及三名与本党立场不一致的共和党人的支持。

sentences.en: Senators Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, and Mitt Romney of Utah.
sentences.zh: 他们是来自缅因州的苏珊·柯林斯、阿拉斯加州的丽莎·穆尔科斯基和犹他州的米特·罗姆尼。

sentences.en: In our nation's history, 115 individuals have been confirmed by this body to serve on the Supreme Court of the United States.
sentences.zh: 在我们国家的历史上，有115人被该机构确认在最高法院任职。

sentences.en: Of those, 108 have been white men.
sentences.zh: 其中，108人是白人男性。

sentences.en: Only four have been women.
sentences.zh: 只有四人是女性。

sentences.en: Only two have been African-American.
sentences.zh: 只有两人是非裔美国人。

sentences.en: But Ketanji Brown Jackson will be the first African-American woman ever to hold the title of justice.
sentences.zh: 但凯坦吉·布朗·杰克逊将是第一位获得大法官头衔的非裔美国女性。

sentences.en: In a speech from the Senate floor, Democratic Majority Leader Chuck Schumer called it a long-overdue moment.
sentences.zh: 在参议院发言时，民主党多数党领袖查克·舒默称这是一个迟来的时刻。

sentences.en: Think about the impact that we'll have on our democracy.
sentences.zh: 想想这对我们的民主将产生的影响。

sentences.en: Untold millions of kids will open textbooks and see pictures of Justice Jackson among the highest ranks of our public figures.
sentences.zh: 无数的孩子将打开教科书，看到杰克逊大法官的照片出现在我们公众人物的最高行列中。

sentences.en: How many millions of kids in generations past could have benefited from such a role model?
sentences.zh: 过去几代人中有多少千万的孩子本可以从这样的榜样中受益？

sentences.en: Jackson, who replaces Justice Stephen Breyer, is expected to officially join the court at the end of its term, sometime later this summer.
sentences.zh: 接替斯蒂芬·布雷耶大法官的杰克逊预计将于今年夏天晚些时候，在最高法院本届任期结束时正式加入法院。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Stella Tan, Asta Chaturvedi, Jessica Chung, and Chelsea Daniel.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由斯特拉·谭、阿斯塔·查图尔维迪、杰西卡·钟和切尔西·丹尼尔制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans and Paige Cowett, contains original music from Marion Lozano and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威廉斯和佩奇·考特编辑，包含马里昂·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Alicia Ba Etoop.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢艾丽西亚·巴·埃图普。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听关于如何让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是他们睡觉时会不会断片。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光照？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
